title: Walkable ground: one kerb wherever walking ends (forecourt and campus)
caption: Stage 1 of #362. The walk grid and the kerbs now come from one list of walkable ground, so he stops exactly at a kerb, a wall, a building or a gate, never at an invisible line. Beds lie flush with the lawn. Forecourt and campus only; the other places follow after you have seen this. Beds are straight strips along the paths, or plants loose on the lawn; no blob-shaped beds.

sections.title: Campus: beds follow the paths, no blob-shaped beds
sections.caption: Your screenshot was the campus bench court. Every curved bed in the campus is now a straight strip along the path or court it borders, behind its kerb; plants that stood further out stand loose on the lawn.

sections.title: Forecourt: the garden court from the lane (Jørgen's view)
sections.caption: Street-style look, same spot and camera. The stepped plots and the double kerb in the lawn are gone; a kerbed gravel path joins the lane to the court.

sections.title: Walking into the edge
sections.caption: He walks south across the gravel court until he stops. Before, his body ran over the edge; now his feet stop at the kerb.

sections.title: Forecourt: lane and court
sections.caption: The lane's bench bay is paved and walkable with a kerb round it; the north strip lost its extra kerbs; the garden east of the bikes is lawn behind a low wall.

sections.title: Campus garden
sections.caption: Every path and the bench court now has a kerb where it meets lawn; before, most of these edges were invisible walls.

sections.title: Where he can walk, from above
sections.caption: Green is where his centre can stand, red where it can't. The red band is his radius inside each kerb.

sections.title: Campus: the paths to the wing's staff door and bike shelter
sections.caption: Both paths had a kerb across their mouths. Now they are walkable to the door and to the shelter's bikes. Walking toward each: before he stopped at the street's kerb (or went round to the cross street); now he reaches them.
